preamble: The four entries were unofficially shortlisted for the 4 12 21 down

clue.text: Could be ARIA 1100 HELP

indicators.note: 'could be' says the letters that follow might be rearranged into something else

parts.note: in Roman numerals 1100 is M (1000) plus C (100)

explanation.surface: A coded string of letters and digits that looks like a message from a computer screen.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 1100 as the Roman numerals MC, then rearrange ARIA, MC and HELP. The whole clue is also the definition, since the string mixes letters and figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Alphameric describes a string made of both letters and numerals, which is exactly what the clue's own text shows.

clue.text: Frog run logistics require guiding for entry

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are what the other words call for, so 'require' asks for them to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Organising a frog run is an exercise in leading youngsters into a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guiding' is the Girl Guides' movement, which is scouting for girls; 'for entry' points to the preamble: Scouting for Girls is one of the four theme entries, a band shortlisted for the awards.
explanation.definitionFit: Guiding is the girls' version of the scouting movement, so the phrase literally describes it.

clue.text: One taking plunge has time to change course

parts.note: a diver is someone who plunges into water

explanation.surface: A swimmer leaping into the water takes a moment to alter direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To divert is to turn something aside from its route, a synonym for altering course.

clue.text: Student leaves Leghorn to the natives to be in love madly with composer of today

indicators.note: the student departs from the Italian city name, so that letter is taken out of it

parts.note: Livorno is the Italian name for the port the English call Leghorn
L, the learner plate, stands for a student

indicators.note: the departed student goes to be inside the scrambled word that follows
'madly' suggests the word love is to be wildly rearranged

explanation.surface: A pupil abandons an Italian port to fall wildly for a modern songwriter.
explanation.walkthrough: The student who 'leaves' the port does not vanish: 'to be in' sends that same L into the jumbled love. 'Of today' nods to the songwriting awards named after him, presented the day the puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivor Novello was a Welsh songwriter and composer, after whom the British songwriting awards are named.

clue.text: Time went quickly on strip, otherwise I should be bilingual

parts.note: ran means moved quickly
a slat is a narrow strip of wood
or introduces an alternative, meaning otherwise

explanation.surface: Someone muses that if time had not raced along the runway they would speak two languages.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who renders one language into another must know at least two, so the job demands being bilingual.

clue.text: Authority for a vehicle to proceed by river to Southwest African border

parts.note: an OK is approval or authorisation
a van is a road vehicle
go means to proceed

explanation.surface: Permission is granted for a car to drive along a river to a frontier in southern Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: South West Africa is the old name for Namibia, whose northern border the river partly forms.
explanation.definitionFit: The Okavango is the southern African river forming part of Namibia's border before ending in a delta in Botswana.

clue.text: It leaves airline in speechless state

indicators.note: the word it departs from the airline's name, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Alitalia was the Italian national airline
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gets off a plane so stunned they cannot say a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Alalia is a medical term for loss or absence of the power of speech.

clue.text: Forbid check on love

parts.note: to vet is to check thoroughly
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A parent bans any further check on a romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is a refusal of permission; as a verb it means to prohibit.

clue.text: Rider from the West finds water an almost unchanging material

parts.note: a loch is a Scottish lake
Invar is a nickel-steel alloy that barely expands with heat

explanation.surface: A horseman from the west discovers a lake made of a stable substance.
explanation.walkthrough: In Walter Scott's ballad, 'young Lochinvar is come out of the west', riding to claim his bride.
explanation.definitionFit: Lochinvar is the dashing horseman hero of Scott's poem, who comes riding out of the west.

clue.text: Like you, I'm English turning to Australian entry

indicators.note: turning means the words before it are turned into a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe adds no letter

explanation.surface: Someone says that, like their friend, they are an English person becoming Australian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entry' points to the preamble: the Australian singer Kylie Minogue is one of the four shortlisted names.
explanation.definitionFit: Kylie Minogue is the Australian pop singer, one of the four themed entries for the songwriting awards.

clue.text: Arrogance at the heart of the French writer

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, here of the word the

parts.note: auteur is French for author

explanation.surface: Pride lies at the core of a Gallic author's character.
explanation.definitionFit: Hauteur is a haughty, superior manner, a synonym for arrogance.

clue.text: See 4
Article dropped by revolutionary with some fluidity

indicators.note: the article is let go by the revolutionary, so its letter is removed

parts.note: a Maoist is a follower of the Chinese revolutionary Mao
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A grammar point is abandoned by a radical with a somewhat flexible approach.
explanation.definitionFit: Moist means slightly wet, having a little liquid about it.

clue.text: Draw from good food shop undiluted drug

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a shop for fine food
neat means without water or mixer
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone picks up a pure narcotic from a delicatessen.
explanation.definitionFit: To delineate is to draw or trace the outline of something.

clue.text: Get more black and grey, perhaps, to make 15 expand

parts.note: to darken is to become blacker

indicators.note: perhaps hints that grey is only a possible version of the letters, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something turns darker and greyer, maybe, causing a cross-reference to swell.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is EVERYTHING: dark energy is the hypothetical force making the whole universe expand ever faster.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicists invoke this unseen force to explain the accelerating expansion of the cosmos, that is, all there is.

clue.text: Extremely emaciated in (say) repetition needed for entry

indicators.note: the extreme thinness is placed in the abbreviation for say

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as 'say' does
very means extremely
thin describes someone emaciated

explanation.surface: A painfully thin person needs to say something over and over to get in.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme entry is the Manchester band Everything Everything, so the word must be repeated to name it.
explanation.definitionFit: The band shortlisted for the awards is called Everything Everything, the grid word doubled.

clue.text: Charge for putting name down for King's — setting Tate on fire

parts.note: regis is Latin for of the king

indicators.note: setting the gallery alight sends its letters flying into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone enrolling at King's College pays a fee while setting the Tate gallery ablaze.
explanation.walkthrough: Tate is a London art gallery; King's suggests a college.
explanation.definitionFit: A registration fee is the charge paid to put one's name on a list or roll.

clue.text: Yorkshire village from New York — gee! bliss!

indicators.note: from tells us the answer is made from the letters that follow

parts.note: gee is the spelt-out name of the letter G

explanation.surface: An American exclaims with delight on reaching a quiet English village.
explanation.walkthrough: Slingsby is a village in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Slingsby is a small village in Ryedale, North Yorkshire, England.

clue.text: See 2
Rifleman's progress through life outside rubbish dump

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition reads rifleman is

indicators.note: the course of life sits outside the dump, wrapping it

parts.note: a career is one's course through life
a bin is where rubbish is dumped

explanation.surface: A soldier's working life is spent around a refuse tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbineer is a soldier armed with a carbine, a kind of short rifle.

clue.text: Fugitive dropping article under aircraft?

indicators.note: the fugitive drops an article, so that letter goes

parts.note: a runaway is someone who has fled
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An escaped prisoner throws something down beneath a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by location: the strip lies under aircraft as they land.
explanation.definitionFit: A runway is the strip beneath planes as they take off and land.

clue.text: Cheer 'eard to order?

indicators.note: the dropped aitch of 'eard means the cheer is spoken in a Cockney way, without its H

parts.note: hooray is a cheer

explanation.surface: A shout of approval is heard in a Cockney accent as a command.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the H, as 'eard does, turns HOORAY into 'OORAY, close to the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An array is an ordered arrangement, as troops in battle order.

clue.text: Struggle to fill commercial breaks with prizes

indicators.note: the struggle is put in to fill the gaps between programmes

parts.note: ads are advertisements shown in commercial breaks
war is a struggle

explanation.surface: A battle fills the ad breaks during an awards show.
explanation.definitionFit: Awards are honours or trophies given in recognition, the same thing as prizes.

clue.text: See 10
Setter holding piece reaches peak

indicators.note: the setter holds the piece inside

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as me
op is short for opus, a musical work or piece

explanation.surface: A setter clutching an item climbs to the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peak' is not the summit but the old verb meaning to droop or look sickly, as in peaky.
explanation.definitionFit: To peak in the obsolete sense was to languish or pine, the same as to sulk listlessly.

clue.text: Live author, hard to follow like the Jabberwock slayer

parts.note: be means to exist or live
Kingsley or Martin Amis, both novelists
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A living writer finds it hard to match the hero of a nonsense poem.
explanation.walkthrough: In Lewis Carroll's Jabberwocky, the slayer is hailed as 'my beamish boy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's poem calls the Jabberwock's killer a beamish boy, meaning radiant and beaming.

clue.text: Concoction of phrase and fable?

parts.note: a mixed drink, suggested by the reference book ... Dictionary of Phrase and Fable, which belongs to one who makes it

explanation.definitionFit: A brew is a mixture or concoction, and Brewer compiled the Dictionary of Phrase and Fable.

clue.text: Back of a record: note — Tina doesn't have one entry

indicators.note: back of says the following pieces are read backwards

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record
NB stands for nota bene, note well

explanation.surface: On the flip side of a disc, a memo says a singer has no alternative.
explanation.walkthrough: TINA is the Thatcher slogan There Is No Alternative, so it has no fallback; 'entry' points to the preamble: Plan B is a British rapper.
explanation.definitionFit: A backup strategy is needed only if there is an alternative, which the slogan TINA denies.

clue.text: Girl to go, about to go to boy

indicators.note: about means the second go goes round the first

parts.note: taken as written
to wend is to go on one's way
Len is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl must leave; about to leave, she goes to a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: Gwendolen is the heroine of Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest.
explanation.definitionFit: Gwendolen is a female first name, as for Wilde's Gwendolen Fairfax.
